about: What a correct lens proposes on the Pebble Shop fixture (must: true) and what it must not (decoy: true). Scored by skill/scripts/lib/score.mjs: an emitted card is assigned to the one item its anchors land on most strongly (`anchor` is the primary, `also` the other files a correct card may anchor on; `also` may name a file the finding says is missing). Hypotheses are the H-numbers of each pack as of lens_version 0.1.0 (0.2.0 keeps them). Primary anchor paths are unique within a lens. Each lens seeds more real findings than its budget of 4, so it is judged on choosing: `priority` 1 must be in the top 4, 2 is good, 3 is minor, grounded in what the evidence shows (ticket counts and spread, user-facing or internal, severity). The fixture's direction (_sources.json `directions`) shapes each lens: the item with `focus_by_direction` is the priority-2 one the focus should pull into the top 4; the one with `excluded_by_direction` is a real finding the exclude rules out, so proposing it is a direction violation.

items.why: trackingUrl already builds the carrier's tracking link, but only the printed packing slip uses it; getOrder leaves carrier and tracking code out of what customers see. Eight tickets from seven customers (SHOP-181 to SHOP-197; SHOP-194 is SHOP-183 again), all component Shipping and label where-is-my-order, arrived in the last five weeks - the strongest and fastest-growing ask, visible only through the labels, components and created_at (the titles rarely say 'tracking'). Serves goal G-1 (order status without support).

toCsv already writes orders as CSV but only the nightly finance job calls it; SHOP-101, SHOP-104 and SHOP-109 ask for an order export over three months (SHOP-113 is SHOP-101's customer again) and goal G-1 names records for bookkeeping.

Guest checkout is built but off unless an owner sets PEBBLE_GUEST_CHECKOUT=1; shoppers leave at 'Sign in to pay' (SHOP-140, SHOP-144) and an owner cannot find the switch (SHOP-170). Serves goal G-2, which is at risk. Fewer tickets than tracking or export.

Customers write to support to get a receipt resent (SHOP-131, SHOP-135, SHOP-138); resendReceipt does it in one call but only the admin CLI reaches it. Serves goal G-1. Three tickets: below tracking and export, and the direction's focus on self-service receipts pulls it into the top 4.

listOrders already takes a status filter, but the GET /orders route never passes one; SHOP-120, SHOP-124 and SHOP-127 ask to filter the order history by status. A convenience with three tickets and no goal behind it: minor next to the rest.

pauseBox(userId, months) already pauses a box for any number of months, but the only caller fixes it at 3; SHOP-190, SHOP-193 and SHOP-196 ask to skip one month. Real, but the direction excludes Pebble Box subscription features.
An exported bulk function reached only from the admin CLI - but admin-only by design (its comment says prices never change from the storefront) and no ticket asks for it.
Looks like an internal helper with no route, but GET /search?suggest=1 already exposes it and docs/api.md documents it.

Three tickets ask to save products for later (SHOP-61, SHOP-66, SHOP-72), but they predate 1.3.0, which shipped it: POST /wishlist is routed, docs/api.md documents it and SHOP-79 thanks the team. Demand that is already met.

A declined card resets the checkout form and shows 'Something went wrong. Please try again later.' with no cause and no next step; SHOP-142 gave up and ordered elsewhere, SHOP-146 retyped the card three times. Lost sales on the step goal G-2 measures.

Subscribing is one click; cancelling is four steps with a fake countdown and a pre-ticked 'pause instead' box that turns a cancel into a pause (SHOP-150, SHOP-153). People keep paying against their choice.

After a pause the pay step says 'Your session expired. Your cart is still here - sign in to continue.', but session() starts a new session id and the cart rows are keyed by the old one, so the cart is gone. Six tickets labelled cart-lost (SHOP-182 to SHOP-195), all component Checkout, in five weeks: the largest cluster, visible as one problem only through the labels and created_at. Goal G-2.

Card logos without alt text (1.1.1), inputs with placeholders but no labels (1.3.1, 3.3.2), a pay control that is a div with onclick and an unlabelled icon (2.1.1, 4.1.2), a red dot as the only status (1.4.1); SHOP-157 and SHOP-158. Two tickets against six for the lost cart; the direction's focus on checkout accessibility pulls it into the top 4.

Save address fires a fetch and ignores the answer: no progress, no 'Address saved.' (the server sends it), no error for an incomplete address; SHOP-161 and SHOP-164. Annoying but nothing is lost: minor.
A bad row stops the price import with an uncaught stack trace after earlier rows were already written, and nothing says which (SHOP-178). Real, but the direction excludes the pebble admin CLI.
An error path that does recover: the cart keeps its contents, the message says how to make room, and it links to the cart.
An empty state that offers two ways forward (show all products, search).
Looks like the checkout page's markup, but here the logo has alt text, the search input has a label and the icon button has aria-label.
A fetch on click like the address form's, but this one disables the button, shows 'Saving...', then the server's message in a status region, and a recovery message when the request fails.

The CLI guide (and the OPS-space runbook PAGE-301) still tells owners to cron `pebble orders sync`; the command and src/jobs/orders-sync.js were removed in a commit 60 days ago (SHOP-172). Owners' nightly accounting push fails every night.

PAGE-312 in the OPS space tells owners to put their merchant key in STONEPAY_KEY and says the shop reads it at start-up; no code reads STONEPAY_KEY - charges use the key committed in src/config.js. Owners believe their key is in use. Only the Confluence page (direction spaces OPS) shows the claim.
The configuration guide documents MAX_CART_ITEMS default 50; src/config.js defaults to 20 since the commit that lowered the cart limit (SHOP-175).
A commit 25 days ago added guest checkout behind PEBBLE_GUEST_CHECKOUT; no doc mentions the variable (SHOP-170 asks how to turn it on).

The POST /cart curl example sends `qty`; addToCart reads `quantity`, so the example silently adds 1 item instead of 2. No ticket yet; the direction's focus on the storefront API reference pulls it into the top 4.
The supplier-sheet guide's JSON uses `amount`; bulkUpdatePrices reads `price`, so the example stops at the first row. Real, but the direction excludes the price import guide.
The README's claims hold: port 8080 by default, PORT overrides it, npm ci / npm start / npm test / npm run seed exist, the linked docs exist.
Mentions `pebble orders sync`, but as history: 1.3.0 added it and 1.4.0 records its removal. Not a ghost feature.
The resend command and its output match cli/pebble.js and resendReceipt exactly.
Shows `pebble orders sync` in a cron line, but for 1.3, which still gets fixes, and tells 1.4 owners what replaces it. Correct for a supported path.

lodash is pinned at 4.17.15, a runtime dependency; the captured npm audit (via `dowser deps`) lists GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm (high, command injection via template) and GHSA-p6mc-m468-83gw (high); the receipt mailer calls _.template. Without the audit output there is no H1 card.
The q query parameter of a public, unauthenticated endpoint is concatenated into a SELECT ... LIKE string; db.query runs it unparameterised.
A live StonePay merchant key (psk_live_...) is committed in src/config.js and sent as the bearer token on every charge.

The shop ships to self-hosting owners (README, release workflow), but there is no SECURITY.md, no security.txt and no disclosure contact anywhere. An absence claim (medium confidence at most), below the three concrete flaws; the direction's focus on CRA readiness pulls it into the top 4.

The results page reads q from the address bar and writes it into the heading with innerHTML, so a crafted link runs script on the shop's origin. Real and user-reachable, but it needs a victim to follow a link: below the injectable SQL and the live key.
`pebble report nightly --since` concatenates its argument into the SQL; only staff on the shop server run it. Real but minor, and the direction excludes the staff admin CLI and its report jobs.
Matches the secret grep (api_key = '...'), but it is a stand-in for a fake server in a unit test and opens nothing.
child_process.execFileSync with constant arguments (git rev-parse --short HEAD): a sink with no user input.
innerHTML is assigned a constant string; product data goes through createElement and textContent.
The release workflow already produces a CycloneDX SBOM and publishes it with each release.

The audit lists minimist 1.2.5 as critical (GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h), but it is a devDependency (lockfile dev: true) used only by the demo seed script, which parses the developer's own arguments; package.json `files` and `npm sbom --omit dev` keep it out of what ships.
